raw:
“I remember a family photograph that was ruined in a flood. It was wet and lying on a towel to dry. That’s the part I keep coming back to—the photograph on the towel, and the stain across my father’s picture. I wanted to look at his face, but my eye kept going to the stain instead.

“It’s funny how a photograph is just paper until something happens to it. Usually you look at the people, not the paper. Then suddenly you’re looking at the damage, wondering what will still be there when it dries. That made me sad. It was still our family photograph, but it wasn’t the same anymore. I don’t remember who else was there clearly. I remember that towel much better.”
